Incorporating the November 2017 Beige Book into the December 13 FOMC statement assessment: The Beige Book broadly corroborates the Committee’s “solid” activity and “strong” labor market narrative. Districts reported modest-to-moderate growth through October–mid-November, tight labor markets with notable wage gains in professional, technical, and production roles, firm consumer spending in retail and autos, and a favorable holiday sales outlook. Hurricane rebuilding boosted construction demand and pushed up construction-material costs, adding to near-term price pressures. These details tilt the outlook modestly more positive for growth and gradually firmer inflation than the statement’s cautious tone implies. That said, the October SLOOS still flags mixed credit conditions—tighter terms and softer demand in consumer credit and some investment-related loan categories—arguing for continued “gradual” hikes. Net effect: slightly more constructive than neutral.
